# Scaffold From Spec

Run **after** `bootstrap-repo` (AGENTS.md, `repo-config.md` and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` must exist). Wherever this skill says `ARCHITECTURE.md` (including `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`), read "the design doc the spec requires, if it names one (e.g. `SOLUTION.md`)". **In this repo that is `SOLUTION.md`; the implementation plan is `ai/implementation-plan.md` and the conformance table is `ai/spec-conformance.md` (the spec reserves `ai/` for AI working artifacts); wherever this skill says `docs/implementation-plan.md` or `docs/spec-conformance.md`, use those paths.** Every deliverable the spec lists must be built and verified, not just the code. Builds the project as an ordered list of **vertical slices** (thin end-to-end flows), each built, tested and verified before the next.

## Flow
There is one flow, no modes: get the plan approved, build the foundation slice and **pause once** for the user to confirm it (it becomes the reference implementation every later slice copies), then build the remaining slices in order without asking. Stop early only on a failing build/test you can't fix, a blocking question, a spec conflict or an unmeetable domain constraint. If the user asks to pause after every slice (or to build one slice only), do that.

Resume by re-running: the skill reads `docs/implementation-plan.md` and continues from the first unchecked slice.

## Preconditions
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` has no blocking open questions. If it does, stop and ask the user to decide them (ask_user).
- Working tree is clean or the user accepts new files. Do not commit.

## Preflight (first run, before the foundation slice)
Confirm the toolchain can actually build: SDK/runtime matches the pinned version and the spec's target (report any mismatch, e.g. spec says a newer runtime than is installed), the package feed resolves, and `.editorconfig` exists or is planned. If a user- or machine-level package config points at a private feed that fails restore, write a repo-level config that clears inherited sources (e.g. `NuGet.Config` with `<clear/>` plus the public feed) before the foundation slice. Record mismatches as assumptions in the plan. If the default SDK differs from the spec's target (e.g. a preview SDK installed for a stable target), propose pinning the version (e.g. `global.json`) before the foundation slice.

## Steps
1. **Read** the spec, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (especially "Domain constraints" and "Pack overrides"), and every `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` whose `applyTo` matches the files you will create (dotnet, dotnet-api, messaging-services, observability, database-postgres, testing). Packs are general defaults; spec constraints win — report any conflict. **Stop if `ARCHITECTURE.md` "Decisions" contains any `OPEN` item**: list them and send the user back to the `bootstrap-repo` Architecture decisions step.
2. **Plan** (first run only): write `docs/implementation-plan.md`: projects/modules and dependency direction, tooling to use (`dotnet new`, `npm create`, etc.), and an **ordered slice list** (give each slice a descriptive kebab-case name, e.g. `foundation-and-auth`, `create-link`, `redirect-and-expiry`, not S1/S2; refer to domain constraints by name too, e.g. `never-block-redirect`, `no-visitor-data`) covering every functional requirement in the spec — the first slice is always the foundation plus the thinnest end-to-end flow, named for what it contains (e.g. `foundation-and-create-link`, never `slice-1`); each later slice names the spec requirements it covers, its dependencies and its tests. Use checkboxes for status. **Before showing it, have the `planner` agent critique the plan** (ordering, coverage of every spec requirement, where each constraint is built and tested) and fix or flag its findings. Show it and **wait for approval of the plan.** Before asking, **print** the "Diagram" from `ARCHITECTURE.md` in the console next to the slice list (create it now if bootstrap skipped it); don't just point at the file. The user should see the target shape and which slice builds which part; mark each slice's parts on it.
3. **Foundation** (inside the foundation slice): generate structure with the ecosystem's own tooling rather than hand-writing project files. Pin versions centrally if the pack says so. Add `.editorconfig`, `.gitignore`, and CI skeleton only if the spec/repo-config calls for them. Make `.editorconfig` agree with the testing pack and `dotnet format --verify-no-changes`: relax the rules that clash with its test naming (e.g. CA1707 underscores in test names, CA1848 logger delegates), make constants PascalCase and static readonly private fields `_`-prefixed (a PascalCase-const rule must outrank the `_camelCase` private-field rule), and watch for CA1001 on test classes owning disposables. Run format once on the generated code before ticking the foundation slice.
4. **Implement the slice** inside the architecture: boundary adapter → typed command/query → handler → port → infrastructure adapter. Stub external systems behind interfaces; no speculative features, no extra layers.
5. **Wire composition root**: DI registrations, configuration binding, logging, health endpoint, migrations folder (if a DB is in scope) with a new versioned migration.
6. **Tests**: at least one unit test per handler/validator/mapper in the slice, plus an integration test (tagged per repo-config) if infra is involved. Add or extend a DI smoke test where the stack supports it.
7. **Align pack paths** (first slice only): if a pack's `applyTo` globs don't match the created folder names, adjust **only the globs** (never the rules) and report it. Fill or remove `{{…}}` template slots the spec doesn't cover (e.g. delete the tenant slot if there is no tenancy). Spec-specific rules belong in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, not in the packs.
8. **Verify the slice (gate):** run restore, build and the unit tests from `AGENTS.md`; fix failures; run lint/format. Never start the next slice on a red build. Then **check the slice against `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` "Domain constraints" and "Pack overrides"**: for each constraint the slice touches, state in the report whether it is satisfied and where (file/test); if none apply, say so. Fix violations before ticking the slice; if a constraint can't be met, stop and ask. Update the commands table in `AGENTS.md` if a command turned out wrong, and update `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` / project index with what was created (port and type names in its "Shape" section drift from the code, so re-read it against the code each slice) (see `docs-maintenance.instructions.md`). Tick the slice in `implementation-plan.md`. **Independent review** (every slice): before ticking, run the `code-reviewer` agent on the slice's diff as a fresh-context reader, giving it `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and the spec requirements the slice covers; fix or report what it finds. If the folder is not a git repo (no diff), review the slice's files with a general-purpose reviewer agent (e.g. `rubber-duck`) instead; this found a real startup-validation bug and an SSRF bypass in test runs.
9. **Report per slice** (and a final summary at the end): what was created, what is stubbed, how each claim was verified, assumptions, unverified items, next slice. After the foundation slice, stop and ask the user to confirm it; after any later slice, continue unless a stop condition applies. Do **not** commit.
10. **Final spec-conformance check** (after the last slice is ticked): run the build, unit tests and format/lint once more on the final result, then have the `planner` agent (read-only, strongest model) compare the whole project to the spec. Give it the spec, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/implementation-plan.md` and the code. It returns a **traceability table**: every functional requirement, non-functional requirement and domain constraint mapped to the code that implements it and the test that proves it, each marked `met`, `partial`, `missing` or `unverifiable` (say why). It also lists anything built that the spec doesn't ask for. Save the table as `docs/spec-conformance.md`, show it in the console, and **fix nothing silently**: for each `partial`/`missing` item, propose a new slice or ask the user to accept it as deferred. Do not call the project done while any item is `missing` and unaccepted.

## Hardening slice (last slice; decide and record, don't force)
Cover only what the spec requires, and for each item either do it or record it as deferred with a reason: retention/immutability checks for stored data; a production guard on any fake/stub adapter; correlation ids in logs; bounded metric tags (no unbounded ids); a success log per key handler; and correlation ids in logs. List deferred items (auth, transport security, alerting owners, untested worker loops) in the plan.

## Rules
- Never invent requirements; if the spec is silent, choose the simplest option and list it under "Assumptions" in the report.
- Prefer the repo's reference implementation (`repo-config.md`) once one exists; the first slice you build becomes it — record it there and ask the user to confirm.
- Don't pull in packages/frameworks that the spec or architecture didn't name without asking.
- Slices run **sequentially by default** (they share files and interfaces). Run independent slices in parallel, on separate branches/worktrees, only if the user asks, and merge afterwards.
- If a later slice invalidates an earlier decision, stop, explain, and ask rather than silently reworking finished slices.
